A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching title, authors, and core classification experiments. Text, tables, and rendered figures support reliable comparison. v2 contains no appendices; v3 includes readable Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v2 reports original repeated-run classification experiments across eight datasets, including F1 scores, performance variability, and break-even sample counts in Figure 2 and Table 2.

after.justification: v3 reports original classification experiments and additional model and quantisation comparisons, including the results in Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same four learning approaches: fine-tuning, prompting, in-context learning, and instruction-tuning, retaining full Flan-T5 tuning and LoRA for Mistral/Zephyr. No new learning algorithm or architecture is introduced. Changes concern experimental configurations and newly documented implementation details.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same eight English classification datasets: SST2, MRPC, CoLA, BoolQ, AG News, TREC, SNIPS, and DB Pedia. Quantisation and example-count experiments retain these tasks and populations; they change settings rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 replaces the ChatGPT 3.5-turbo-0613 comparator with GPT-4o-mini-2024-07-18 and adds LLaMA-3 8B Instruct for prompting and in-context learning. These models participate in the reported comparisons, including Figure 5, substantially updating the general-model comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 fixes in-context learning at two examples per class; v3 varies the count within context limits and reports the best performance available up to each dataset size. Appendix A.1 reports subsampling from one example per class instead of ten total. v3 also introduces full-precision controls, selects between precision settings, and adds FLOP-based resource comparisons.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds controlled comparisons of four-bit and full-precision Mistral/Zephyr, examining performance and variability. Figure 7 adds example-count sensitivity curves showing performance collapses. Existing model-size and failure-mode discussion largely moves to Appendix B, where it is extended with findings about the benefits of additional examples.

E5.justification: The stated run counts remain 100 for fine-tuning, 20 otherwise, and 10 for GPT, with controlled seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting. v3 supplements this with distributional boxplots in Figure 6 and explicitly documents the mean-minus-SD versus mean-plus-SD comparison for variance-aware crossings. No increase in repeated-run counts is established.

E6.justification: Break-even values and performance curves are substantially revised, with additional model, quantisation, and compute results. For AG News, RoBERTa versus Flan-T5 in-context learning changes from 350/1100 labels in v2 Table 2 to 300/800 in v3 Appendix B. The in-context protocol changes, so this is not a same-setting improvement. Detailed model-by-size thresholds are also replaced by best-approach results in v3 Table 1.

T1.justification: The average-performance and variance-aware break-even concepts are retained. v3 explains their operational comparison more explicitly, but introduces no new formal assumptions, theoretical propositions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central small-model competitiveness claim remains, but v3 changes the abstract's typical-label statement from 10–1000 to 100 on average and broadens the contribution to compute efficiency and quantisation. Negligible quantisation impact becomes a headline finding, and the claimed extreme effect of variance is reframed around the revised results.

C2.justification: v3 adds possible pretraining contamination as an explanation and explicitly acknowledges that contamination is unverified. It expands interpretations concerning context limits, example quality, inference costs, and quantisation tradeoffs. Recommendations now address prompt/example optimisation and reduce the suggested average fine-tuning annotation requirement from approximately 1000 to 100 samples.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents the Hugging Face SFT trainer, completion-only training collator, approach-specific use of dataset subsets, and model/dataset-specific precision selection. It also supplies computation estimates and their scope. Existing prompts, most training hyperparameters, the code-access link, and hardware/emissions information are retained or relocated rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: The central comparison literature remains, with targeted additions concerning quantisation, prompt/sample selection, and contamination, including Jin et al. (2024), Liu et al. (2024), and Li and Flanigan (2024). These extend the positioning toward compute efficiency and sensitivity without replacing the original research context.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganises the narrative: Section 3 becomes an explicit comparison methodology, recommendations become a separate discussion section, and experimental details, model-size analysis, and emissions material move into appendices. The abstract, contribution list, methodology explanations, and recommendations are extensively revised.

P2.justification: The detailed all-model plot in v2 Figure 2 is redrawn and expanded as v3 Figure 5, alongside new best-model and size-group summaries. v3 adds a dataset-dependence figure, quantisation boxplots and sensitivity curves, and a FLOP table. The break-even table is substantially condensed; the prompt table is relocated to Appendix A.

improvement.justification: The variable-shot experiments and full-precision controls address important untested dependencies in v2's fixed-shot, quantised-model comparisons, substantially strengthening the evidence behind the central break-even analysis. Expanded implementation details and compute estimates also make the recommendations more auditable. The condensed table loses exact model-specific thresholds, and broad quantisation claims understate some exceptions visible in Figure 6, but these drawbacks are outweighed by the stronger controls and transparency.
